questions.prompt: Where does a SELECT execute?
questions.explanation: SSMS sends the batch to the database engine.

questions.prompt: What does GO do?
questions.explanation: SSMS recognizes GO; the engine does not execute it as T-SQL.

questions.prompt: What identifies an order line?
questions.explanation: The composite primary key prevents the same product appearing twice on one order.

questions.prompt: How do products relate to orders?
questions.explanation: OrderItems stores each order/product association and its quantity.

questions.prompt: Which predicate finds missing cities?
questions.explanation: Equality with NULL evaluates to unknown, not true.

questions.prompt: Which type stores an exact unit price?
questions.explanation: decimal stores fixed precision and scale without floating-point approximation.

questions.prompt: Which clause filters individual rows?
questions.explanation: WHERE filters rows before aggregation.

questions.prompt: Does SELECT guarantee insertion order?
questions.explanation: A result has no guaranteed order without ORDER BY.

questions.prompt: What makes TOP deterministic?
options: ORDER BY with a unique tie-breaker
questions.explanation: Ordering resolves both the sorting rule and tied positions.

questions.prompt: Which syntax pages T-SQL rows?
options: ORDER BY … OFFSET 2 ROWS FETCH NEXT 2 ROWS ONLY
questions.explanation: OFFSET/FETCH is part of ORDER BY in T-SQL.

questions.prompt: Why avoid an end timestamp of 23:59:59?
options: Later fractional seconds may be excluded
questions.explanation: A next-day exclusive boundary includes all supported time precision.

questions.prompt: Which predicate keeps the column unwrapped?
questions.explanation: An unwrapped range predicate can support an index seek.

questions.prompt: What is the result grain here?
questions.explanation: Each order joins to its single customer.

questions.prompt: Why can Ada appear twice?
questions.explanation: Repeating parent attributes is expected at child grain.

questions.prompt: Which count returns zero for an unmatched customer?
questions.explanation: The unmatched right-side key is NULL and COUNT(column) skips it.

questions.prompt: Where can a child filter preserve all customers?
questions.explanation: A filter in ON limits matches while retaining unmatched left rows.

questions.prompt: Which customer has no orders?
questions.explanation: Cora has order 104; Emi has no related row.

questions.prompt: Does SELECT 1 mean EXISTS counts one row?
options: It limits the query to one row
No; it tests whether any row exists
questions.explanation: EXISTS tests existence, not the projected value.

questions.prompt: Two lines joined to two payments produce how many rows?
questions.explanation: Each line matches both payments: 2 × 2.

questions.prompt: What fixes the grain?
options: Aggregate each child per order first
questions.explanation: Preaggregation produces one row per order on both sides.

questions.prompt: Which clause filters a SUM result?
questions.explanation: HAVING is evaluated for grouped results.

questions.prompt: Why group by CustomerID too?
questions.explanation: CustomerID defines the customer even when names repeat.

questions.prompt: What does CASE return when no WHEN matches and no ELSE exists?
questions.explanation: The implicit ELSE value is NULL.

questions.prompt: What grain does this aggregate return?
questions.explanation: There is no GROUP BY, so the full input is one group.

questions.prompt: How long is a CTE name in scope?
questions.explanation: A CTE is scoped to one statement.

questions.prompt: Does a CTE guarantee a stored intermediate result?
questions.explanation: The optimizer can expand the expression into the surrounding plan.

questions.prompt: Which APPLY preserves customers without orders?
questions.explanation: OUTER APPLY adds a NULL-extended result when there is no match.

questions.prompt: Why order the TOP subquery?
options: To define which order is latest
questions.explanation: TOP alone cannot identify a deterministic latest order.

questions.prompt: Does a window COUNT collapse rows?
questions.explanation: A window expression adds a value to each input row.

questions.prompt: What does PARTITION BY CustomerID define?
questions.explanation: Each customer gets a separate window partition.

questions.prompt: Which function finds a second distinct score?
questions.explanation: DENSE_RANK = 2 represents the second distinct ordered value.

questions.prompt: What rank follows a two-way tie for first with RANK?
questions.explanation: RANK leaves a gap for the other row occupying the tied position.

questions.prompt: What is LAG’s default for a missing preceding row?
questions.explanation: Without a supplied default, LAG returns NULL outside the partition.

questions.prompt: Which frame expresses cumulative rows?
questions.explanation: It starts at the first row and ends at the current row.

questions.prompt: Which operator retains duplicates?
questions.explanation: UNION ALL concatenates results without duplicate elimination.

questions.prompt: What does EXCEPT return?
options: Distinct rows only in the left input
questions.explanation: EXCEPT is a distinct set difference.

questions.prompt: Where can a local temp table be accessed?
options: Its owning session, subject to scope
questions.explanation: Local temporary tables are isolated between sessions.

questions.prompt: Are table variables guaranteed to stay entirely in memory?
questions.explanation: They may use tempdb; choose based on measured workload behavior.

questions.prompt: What does an ordinary view store?
options: A frozen copy of the rows
questions.explanation: The engine executes the stored definition when the view is queried.

questions.prompt: Where should result ordering be specified?
options: In the SELECT reading the view
questions.explanation: The consuming query needs ORDER BY for a guaranteed order.

questions.prompt: What is @CustomerID?
questions.explanation: T-SQL procedure parameters carry typed input values.

questions.prompt: Does NOCOUNT ON suppress SELECT results?
questions.explanation: It suppresses row-count messages while retaining selected result sets.

questions.prompt: What does an inline table-valued function return?
questions.explanation: It exposes a parameterized relational expression.

questions.prompt: Which object fits a data-changing workflow?
questions.explanation: T-SQL UDFs cannot modify persistent database state.

questions.prompt: Does IDENTITY alone enforce uniqueness?
questions.explanation: A PRIMARY KEY or UNIQUE constraint enforces uniqueness.

questions.prompt: Does CHECK (Quantity > 0) alone reject NULL?
questions.explanation: CHECK rejects false; unknown passes. NOT NULL handles missing values.

questions.prompt: Which OUTPUT image holds the previous value?
questions.explanation: deleted contains the prior image for UPDATE or DELETE.

questions.prompt: What does a missing UPDATE WHERE do?
questions.explanation: Without a filter every row is targeted, subject to constraints and triggers.

questions.prompt: What does XACT_STATE() = -1 mean?
questions.explanation: The transaction can only be fully rolled back.

questions.prompt: Should an application silently swallow every database error?
options: No; clean up and report or rethrow
questions.explanation: Callers need to know the operation failed.

questions.prompt: What does rowversion represent?
questions.explanation: It changes when the row is updated; it does not encode wall-clock time.

questions.prompt: What should a zero-row optimistic update trigger in the application?
options: Handle a conflict or missing row
questions.explanation: The row may have changed or disappeared since it was read.

questions.prompt: A statement updates 20 rows. How often does its DML trigger execute?
questions.explanation: The trigger executes once with all affected rows in its transition tables.

questions.prompt: Does rollback also undo the trigger’s audit inserts?
questions.explanation: Trigger writes are part of the triggering transaction.

questions.prompt: Does every new index improve every workload?
options: No; writes and storage also cost work
questions.explanation: Index usefulness depends on reads, writes, selectivity, and the execution plan.

questions.prompt: What is a filtered index?
options: An index on a subset selected by a predicate
An index that forces all queries to filter
questions.explanation: Its predicate limits which base rows have index entries.

questions.prompt: Does an actual execution plan require executing the query?
questions.explanation: Actual runtime information is collected during execution.

questions.prompt: What does STATISTICS IO expose?
questions.explanation: Its Messages output helps compare database I/O work.

questions.prompt: Which is generally friendlier to a date index?
questions.explanation: The range exposes usable start/end values for an index search.

questions.prompt: What should be checked before declaring a rewrite faster?
questions.explanation: A fast wrong query is not a successful optimization.

questions.prompt: Does row-versioned read committed prevent all writer blocking?
questions.explanation: Writers can still contend on the same rows.

questions.prompt: Why is NOLOCK unsuitable as a general correctness fix?
options: It can read uncommitted or inconsistent data
questions.explanation: Fewer read locks do not imply correct or consistent answers.

questions.prompt: What is the correct overall outstanding balance?
questions.explanation: 815 non-cancelled sales minus 205 payments equals 610.

questions.prompt: Where should cancelled orders be excluded to preserve all customers?
options: In the per-order relation before the LEFT JOIN
With a final WHERE o.Status condition on unmatched rows
questions.explanation: Filtering the child relation preserves customers with no eligible orders.
